title: Discovery candidate peer
description:
An advisory reachability observation: this PeerId was seen at these addresses, by this provider, at this time. It grants NOTHING — not trust, not membership, not liveness. Dialing it still requires PeerTrustPolicy authorization and passes the root DialAdmissionGate (ADR-0010, ADR-0011, ADR-0012).

WHAT IS ABSENT IS ENFORCED. `EndpointId`, ChannelIds, application roles, membership, and human presence are explicitly outside discovery and must never become candidate metadata (ADR-0009, DISCOVERY.md). `additionalProperties: false` is what stops one being added later as an obvious convenience — the DHT and the discovery layer are exactly where such a field would leak routing or presence to anyone who can query.

There is deliberately no `confidence` field: a low/normal/configured scale duplicates provenance and reads as trust, which is the one thing a candidate must never imply.

items.description: An opaque reachability address. Opaque on purpose: the neutral contract does not commit to multiaddr syntax, and a backend-specific format must not leak upward (§4).

source.description: The provider name. Provenance is how candidate quality is judged, which is why it is required rather than optional.

expires_at.description: Absent means the provider does not model expiry, not that the observation is permanent.

protocol_observations.description: Bounded advisory transport facts learned on AUTHENTICATED connections — for example an exact Identify protocol string. Not trust, not application roles, not capability authorization. Capped at 16 per peer so a peer cannot grow unbounded state in another's cache, and freshness must not outlive the candidate that supplied them. Declared a Set in the normative candidate shape, so `uniqueItems` is asserted like the adjacent addresses set: duplicates would otherwise validate, consume the 16-item cap, and produce a shape a set-modelled implementation cannot round-trip.

protocol_id.description: An opaque protocol identifier, 256 ASCII bytes at most. Compared exactly; never parsed for meaning.
